title: Music of Papua New Guinea - Wikipedia
text: The music of Papua New Guinea encompasses a wide range of traditional and contemporary styles developed across the country's highly diverse ethnic groups. Traditional celebrations known as sing-sing feature communal song and dance, and form a central part of cultural life.

text: Ganglau is an endangered indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: TransNewGuinea.org
text: TransNewGuinea.org is a database of the Trans-New Guinea language family and friends. The Trans-New Guinea language family currently occupies most of the interior of New Guinea. This family is possibly the third largest in the world with 400 languages and is tentatively thought to have originated with root-crop agriculture around 10,000 years ago.
